Truth fix: the guard expression is matched as text, not spliced into a regular expression. bash built
"(long" + "[[:space:]]*>..." for line 8, gawk died on the invalid regexp, the rest of the file (the
literal-zero call on line 9) was never read and the lint still exited 1; "x$y" never matched its own guard
($ is an anchor), so line 6 FAILed although line 5 guards it.
-- args --
@DIR@/t
-- want --
exit 1
FAIL  lint-delays     @DIR@/t/G.java:4  unfloored  cannot verify floor of variable: a.b
PASS  lint-delays     @DIR@/t/G.java:6  guarded at :5
FAIL  lint-delays     @DIR@/t/G.java:8  unfloored  cannot verify floor of variable: (long
FAIL  lint-delays     @DIR@/t/G.java:9  literal-zero  BRelTime(0) — Niagara rejects delay/period <= 0
-- stderr --
-- t/G.java --
class G {
  void a(long x, long[] arr) {
    if (aXb > 0) foo();
    Clock.schedule(this, BRelTime.make(a.b), go, null);
    if (x$y > 0) foo();
    Clock.schedule(this, BRelTime.make(x$y), go, null);
    if ((long) x > 0) foo();
    Clock.schedule(this, BRelTime.make((long) x), go, null);
    Clock.schedule(this, BRelTime.make(0), go, null);
  }
}
